newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Democratic leader praises revised budget.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Democratic leader praises revised budget.

text.p: California's Senate President Bill Lockyer praised Gov. Pete Wilson's new spending plan on Wednesday, but said Democrats want the final budget to include pay raises for state employees.

With state coffers flush with cash, the Republican governor has proposed a $68.2 billion revised 1997-1998 budget, up from the $66.6 billion budget proposed in January. The revised budget would aid cash-strapped local governments, and sharply increase education and child care spending.
Lockyer, a Democrat, welcomed the revisions.

"We are especially gratified that Gov. Wilson has responded, beyond our expectations in some cases, to Democrats' proposals to place a higher priority on state spending for public education and to help the needy move from welfare to work," Lockyer said. "Although some policy differences must still be resolved, we now have good reason to hope for a timely agreement on the final 1997-98 budget."

Wilson's new spending plan would boost education funding by $340 million, providing an additional $230 million to reduce class sizes, $60 million to fund standardized testing, and $50 million for classroom technology.

The budget included a $440 million welfare-to-work plan with funds to pay for new child care programs. Wilson has also proposed to reduce the state's bank and corporations tax rate by 10 percent over the next two years.
Lockyer said the tax cut plan was "excessive and robs schools of too much revenue."
Lockyer was critical of Wilson's proposed welfare grant restrictions, calling them "harmful and unnecessary."
Lockyer said there is enough money in the budget to fund pay raises for state employees. "Resolving this problem is a high priority for Senate Democrats," he said.
